report.summary: Chunk 4 of 8 of daedalus/council/publish.py: implements render_markdown function, rendering council verdict as markdown with load-bearing order.
risks: render_markdown (line 361) | medium | The docstring claims 'Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.' This is uncheckable from this chunk alone; the function calls _text, _field, _as_list, _verbatim, _quorum_counts which may perform I/O. | Check the implementations of those helper functions.

handoff.purpose: Render one council deliberation as markdown with deliberate ordering.

symbols.name: render_markdown
symbols.note: Renders a council verdict to markdown string. Calls helpers _text, _field, _as_list, _verbatim, _quorum_counts.

claims.text: Order is deliberate and load-bearing: outcome and the quorum honesty line lead, so a degraded council is the first thing a reader sees and cannot be skimmed past. Then EVERY dissent verbatim with its author -- BEFORE the convergence, because the dissent is the only part that could not have come from asking one model twice. Then where the vendors converged, evidence digests, per-vendor cost/latency, the deliberation itself, and finally the provenance footer (bus path + chain head) that lets a reader verify all of it offline.
claims.why: The chunk shows only the start of the markdown building (up to evidence digests). The ordering described includes sections not yet seen (per-vendor cost/latency, deliberation, provenance footer). The chunk confirms outcome leads, quorum is early, dissents before convergence, evidence digests after convergence. The rest is uncheckable.

claims.text: Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.
claims.why: The function calls helper functions (_text, _field, _as_list, _verbatim, _quorum_counts) whose implementations are not in this chunk. If those helpers perform I/O, the claim would be broken. Cannot verify from this chunk alone.

claims.text: CONVERGENCE, not 'majority'. A majority is a DECISION; convergence is an OBSERVATION about what the vendors said. The council package carries no approve/reject/score/majority/consensus field on purpose -- absence of the field is the control, not a docstring -- and a rendering that reintroduces the word structurally reintroduces the temptation to read it as a verdict. The legacy aliases are kept only so an older payload still renders.
claims.why: The code uses the variable name 'convergence' and extracts it via _field with aliases including 'majority', 'majority_position'. It renders the section heading 'Where the vendors converged' and adds a disclaimer that convergence is an observation, not a decision. The comment is accurately reflected in the code seen.

claims.text: The advisory banner is UNCONDITIONAL. A verdict arriving without the marker is a contract violation, so we say so instead of quietly rendering it as if it carried authority.
claims.why: The code unconditionally adds the advisory banner line: '**ADVISORY ONLY -- this verdict promotes nothing. THE GATE DECIDES, NOT A MODEL.**' regardless of the advisory field value. Then checks if advisory is not True and adds an additional caution. The claim is verified.

claims.text: A short council is a weaker signal and that must be impossible to miss -- it is a warning block, not a footnote.
claims.why: The code uses a markdown warning block (> [!WARNING]) when answered < requested, with the DEGRADED_QUORUM_MARKER and explanatory text. This matches the claim.

claims.text: DISSENT LEADS. Not a stylistic choice: the dissent is the only content in this document that could not have been produced by asking one model twice. Convergence among vendors with overlapping training data is cheap; the objection is what four egress paths were actually paid for. Rendering it after -- and therefore below -- the agreement makes the informative half read as a footnote to the uninformative half.
claims.why: The code renders dissents before convergence. The section '## Dissents' appears before '## Where the vendors converged'. The claim about ordering is verified.

claims.text: A vendor that did not speak has no content; an empty fence is noise that makes a silent turn look like an empty answer.
claims.why: The code checks `if text:` before appending the verbatim fence. If text is empty, no fence is added. This matches the claim.

observations.what: The function uses helper functions _text, _field, _as_list, _verbatim, _quorum_counts whose implementations are not in this chunk.
The docstring claims the function is pure (no I/O, no network, no gate). The implementation calls helpers that may perform I/O. Cannot verify purity from this chunk.
The comment about ordering mentions sections not present in this chunk (per-vendor cost/latency, deliberation, provenance footer). The chunk only shows up to evidence digests.
The code uses DEGRADED_QUORUM_MARKER which is not defined in this chunk; it must be imported or defined elsewhere.
